newsitem.title: UK: DLR UP AS TRADE ROW FEARS FADE, EUROPEAN STOCK CLIMB.
newsitem.headline: DLR UP AS TRADE ROW FEARS FADE, EUROPEAN STOCK CLIMB.

text.p: The dollar strengthened against the yen as President Bill Clinton managed to soothe fears that a summit of leading industrial nations starting on Friday would become a forum for a U.S.-Japan trade row.
European bourses were higher in early trading on the back of a strong overnight finish on Wall Street. Frankfurt stocks made big gains, helped by the dollar, but London made an unsteady start.

The U.S. currency climbed half a yen as world leaders gathered for the three-day meeting of the Group of Seven (G7) in Denver. Remarks by Clinton helped kill market talk that Washington would criticise Tokyo because of the recent jump in its trade surplus.
Clinton said he was concerned about Japan's large trade surplus with the United States but added that Japan was taking steps to boost domestic demand.

Exchange rates are a touchy issue in Japanese-American relations because a strong dollar helps Tokyo's exports of cars and other goods to the United States but Clinton added that exchange rates should not be used to correct trade balances.

Traders took this as reassurance that Washington would not resort to calls for a weaker dollar to help redress the trade imbalance, as it has done in the past, but they were wary of pushing the dollar aggressively higher until after the G7.
"The market looks very nervous ahead of the G7," said Craig Justham, the deputy manager of foreign exchange at nstalt Bankverein.
The dollar was quoted at 114.55 yen, compared to 114.09 in late trade on Thursday. The U.S. currency also strengthened slightly against the mark.
The stronger dollar helped boost European bourses. Frankfurt got off to a busy start, climbing 1.25 percent to an intra-day high of 3,796.8 points on the 30-share DAX index.

"It looks like today is going to be rather volatile but in the end we should see modest gains for the day," said one head trader at a Stuttgart-based bank. "There's no real end in sight to this rally."
Frankfurt investors were encouraged by the dollar. "The market is more focused on the U.S. right now instead of on domestic factors," said one trader.
London, Europe's biggest bourse, flitted in and out of profit in volatile trade with investors focusing on the mid-morning expiry of index options, seen as a negative factor overhanging the market.
After the expiry, the FTSE 100 index of leading shares showed its relief by heading for higher ground and was 6.4 points up at 4,660.1. "The bulls and the bears were head to
head on expiry and the bulls won," said a dealer. "There was a lot of rolling over and now we can go relatively calmly into next week."

London, which has dropped 140 points in the past week, has been dogged by worries of higher interest rates and fears the new Labour government's first budget on July 2 will contain bad news for investors.
The market has been unsettled by persistent press reports that finance minister Gordon Brown will scrap a tax break on dividend payments to major corporate investors.
In Paris, stocks made useful gains but trade was thin with investors digesting the implications of Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's first major policy address on Thursday.

"There's not a lot of interest or a lot of volume," a broker said. "Although we were expecting some clarifications, a lot of doubt remains. A lot of decisions have been put off to September so uncertainty persists."
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7274 marks and 113.55 yen, compared with 1.7247 and 114.09 in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 6.4 points at 4,660.1.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 15.60 points at 2,755.29.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up up 42.86 at 3792.13.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at 339.55 against 339.75 on Thursday. Silver was barely changed at 4.76.
